title: Short-Form Gaming Content Creator / Video Editor – Plix.gg
description:
# Gaming Content Creator — TikTok / Reels / Shorts



Plix.gg is a browser gaming platform with 72,000+ games and 300K+ monthly visitors.



We're hiring a creator to own our short-form content from idea to upload.



This is not an editing-only role. You will find the games, come up with concepts, record gameplay, shoot real-world footage, edit the videos and prepare them for posting.



Content can include:



* Single-game or multi-game videos

* Gameplay, challenges, memes, POVs and lists

* Laptop/phone videos filmed at schools, cafés, malls, outdoors, etc.

* Voiceover or no voiceover

* Trend-based concepts



We want variety. We do not want the same template repeated every day.



## WHAT YOU DO



* Record irl videos

* Find games on Plix worth making content about

* Create your own hooks and concepts

* Record clean gameplay

* Film good-looking IRL footage when the concept requires it

* Edit 10–40 second TikToks, Reels and Shorts

* Add music, captions and sound design

* Test alternative opening hooks

* Use performance data to improve future videos



You do not need to show your face or use your own voice (you are open to do)



## OUTPUT



7 finished videos per week.



Videos may use one game or several games. We care about retention and views, not forcing every video into the same format.



## WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR



* Strong short-form editing

* Good understanding of hooks and first-3-second retention

* Ability to film attractive real-world footage

* Someone who genuinely understands games

* Comfortable developing ideas independently

* Good sense of pacing, music, text, SFX and visual composition



You need:



* PC/laptop capable of smooth browser-game recording

* Smartphone with a good camera

* Reliable internet

* CapCut, Premiere, DaVinci, Final Cut or similar



## HOURS



No fixed schedule, timezone overlap or time tracking.



Work whenever you want as long as the content is delivered on time.



## PAY



₱65,000/month



Paid monthly via Wise.



Reasonable pre-approved expenses for outside shoots are reimbursed separately.



## HOW TO APPLY



Start your message with PLIX.



Send:



1. 1–3 short-form videos you worked on. Tell us whether you created the concept, filmed it, wrote it and/or edited it.



2. Your editing software, PC specs and phone model.



3. Two video ideas for Plix.gg:



   * 1 gameplay concepts

   * 1 real-world/IRL concepts



Shortlisted applicants receive a paid trial video — ₱1500, paid whether or not we hire you. We require 1 irl video and 1 video edit from plix.gg

description:
Revenue & Partnerships Manager — Serviced Accommodation (Remote)

Company: Accommos Ltd (brands: Accommos, Staymodu, Glowhouse Wellness Stays)

Location: Fully remote — UK business hours (9:00–17:30 GMT/BST)

Type: Full-time contractor 

Compensation: £1,000–£1,400/month base + uncapped commission on incremental revenue + occupancy bonus 

Reports to: Founder / Director



About Accommos

Accommos is a premium, tech-led short-term rental management company operating a portfolio of design-focused apartments across London. Our properties stand apart through wellness amenities — private saunas, cold plunges, hot tubs and cinema rooms — and a strict quality-first operating model. We hold Airbnb Superhost status and run on a modern stack: Guesty, PriceLabs, Enso Connect and heavily automated internal systems.

We are now building the commercial side of the business, and this role owns it end to end: pricing strategy, demand generation, B2B channels, ancillary revenue and guest lifetime value.



The Role

This is not a lead-sourcing or cold-calling position. You will be responsible for maximising total revenue per property across every lever available — rate, occupancy, length of stay, channel mix, ancillary income and repeat business. You will operate like a hotel revenue manager crossed with a commercial partnerships lead.

You will be the first dedicated commercial hire, working directly with the founder. You will have real autonomy, real data access, and compensation tied directly to the revenue you create.



What You Will Own

1. Revenue Management & Pricing Strategy

 -Run event-led pricing: map London demand drivers (concert residencies, stadium

 events, conferences, school holidays, sporting fixtures) months ahead and position rates before the market moves

-Optimise length-of-stay rules: minimum-stay laddering, gap-night and orphan-night auto-discounting, check-in day restrictions that eliminate unsellable one-night gaps

-Segment pricing by demand pattern: mid-week corporate vs. weekend leisure vs. mid- stay relocation, with different rate strategies for each

-Manage the PriceLabs configuration against a monthly RevPAR target per property, not just occupancy

-Run controlled experiments: test rate positions, LOS rules and offer structures, and keep what wins



2. Relocation & Corporate Demand

-Build and manage relationships with relocation agencies, insurance temporary-housing providers, corporate travel bookers, film/TV production companies and serviced- apartment agents

-Register the portfolio with corporate booking agencies and respond to RFPs for corporate housing programmes

-Pursue insurance housing panel placements (temporary accommodation after floods, fires and building failures) — long stays, reliable payers

-Negotiate corporate rates that protect margin while securing the occupancy floor



3. B2B Distribution Channels

-Get the portfolio listed with serviced-apartment agencies and booking platforms that feed corporate demand

-Build direct relationships with travel management companies and executive assistants at Canary Wharf employers

-Develop a location-hire channel for photo and film shoots: agency outreach, rate card, availability process



4. Guest Upsells & Ancillary Revenue

-Design and refine upsell flows for early check-in, late checkout, mid-stay cleaning, extended stays and wellness add-ons through Enso Connect

-Build packaged offers: wellness weekend packages, monthly-stay bundles, celebration set-ups — priced as products, not discounts

-Launch and manage gift vouchers and prepaid stay credits for the direct site Track attach rates per upsell and continuously improve timing, pricing and copy



5. Direct Booking Growth & Lifecycle Marketing

-Grow bookings on our direct website (
), working alongside our paid-ads freelancer

-Own the guest database: post-stay win-back campaigns, seasonal offers to past guests, and a repeat-guest recognition programme that shifts OTA guests to direct

-Build a referral mechanism for guests and corporate contacts

-Recapture lost demand: cancelled bookings, expired quotes and abandoned direct-site sessions get structured follow-up offers

-Improve on-site conversion through offers, copy and booking-journey feedback



6. Occupancy Gap-Filling

-Monitor the portfolio calendar weekly; identify soft periods 2–6 weeks out and act before they arrive

-Sell gaps proactively: outreach to corporate contacts, targeted past-guest offers, location-hire placements, strategic LOS relaxation

-Coordinate all tactics with the pricing strategy so gap-filling never erodes the rate position



KPIs

-RevPAR per property vs. target (the headline metric)

-Incremental revenue generated per month, by stream

-Portfolio occupancy vs. baseline, with rate integrity maintained

-Direct booking share vs. OTA share

-Upsell attach rate and ancillary revenue per booking

-Repeat-guest rate and guest database growth

-Number of active corporate/relocation/agency accounts producing bookings



What We Are Looking For



Must have

-3+ years in revenue management, commercial or business development within short- term rentals, serviced apartments, hotels, corporate housing or relocation services

-Demonstrable record of revenue you personally generated or grew — you will be asked for specifics and numbers

-Working command of revenue metrics: occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, LOS, channel contribution, attach rate

-Excellent spoken and written English; confident and credible on calls with UK corporate clients and agents

-Consultative selling style: you listen, diagnose and propose — you do not script-read Comfortable running structured experiments and reading the results honestly Reliable remote setup: quiet workspace, quality headset, stable internet

-Available during UK business hours



Strongly preferred

-Hands-on experience with dynamic pricing tools (PriceLabs, Wheelhouse, Beyond) and a PMS (Guesty or comparable)

-Existing knowledge of the London accommodation market and its event calendar

-Familiarity with relocation agents, insurance housing, TMCs or serviced-apartment agencies


/CRM lifecycle marketing experience



Compensation Structure

-Base: £1,000–£1,400/month depending on experience

-Commission: percentage of incremental revenue across corporate bookings, upsells, ancillary income and direct bookings (structure shared at interview; uncapped)

-Quarterly RevPAR bonus when the portfolio exceeds target

-Realistic year-one on-target earnings: £20,000–£30,000+



Why This Role Is Worth Your Attention

-Ground-floor commercial hire in a profitable, growing company — you build the function

-Direct line to the founder; decisions in days, not quarters

-A genuinely differentiated product to sell: wellness-led properties that photograph well, review well and command premium rates

-Full access to the levers: pricing, channels, partnerships, marketing — not a narrow patch

-Compensation that scales with the results you deliver



How to Apply

Begin your application with the word “sauna” so we know you read this far. Then include:

1. Your CV

2. A short note (max 200 words) describing one specific piece of revenue you personally created or grew — what it was, how you did it, and the number

3. A voice recording (1–2 minutes, Vocaroo or similar) introducing yourself as if leaving a voi
 for a relocation agent you want to work with



Applications without all three items will not be reviewed.

title: Short-Form Video Editor - Hormozi-Style Content & Motion Graphics (Long-Term Team Role)
description:
WHO WE ARE



MSET is a US marketing agency running paid lead generation for local service businesses. This role edits for MSET itself: our short-form content, our VSLs, our caption-heavy videos. The videos you cut carry real ad spend behind them, so they have to look and feel professional every single time. This is not a churn-out-clips content mill.



READ THIS FIRST



We are hiring a team member, not a gig worker. Someone we can rely on long term, who becomes part of how this agency operates and grows with it. The per-video pay is how we start, not what this is. And this is not a beginner role: if you are new to editing or new to motion graphics, do not apply. You will not pass the test and it will waste your time and ours.



One more thing. This post contains everything we require, and we do not take anyone seriously who applies without reading all of it. Your application will show us whether you did.



THE JOB



We send you raw talking-head footage plus a script or outline. You turn it into a finished Hormozi-style short: kinetic captions synced to the voice, motion graphics that punch the key moments, b-roll and zoom cuts that keep the pace moving, sound design that makes every graphic land. The edit's job is retention: a viewer who meant to scroll past is still watching 40 seconds later.



THE MOTION GRAPHICS BAR



This is the main thing we are hiring for, so here is exactly what we mean by high quality:



- Graphics that serve retention: keyword pops, animated emphasis, icons and visual callouts that hit exactly on the beat of the voice, not floating decoration.

- Clean, professional typography. Deliberate timing. Motion that looks designed, not dragged from a template pack.

- Restraint. The best Hormozi-style edits know when to let a sentence breathe. Wall-to-wall effects is a beginner tell.

- Hand-built work. We are not looking for someone who uses AI to generate these graphics. We can tell the difference, and so can the audience our ad spend is paying to reach. AI-generated graphic work in your portfolio or your test will not pass.



WHAT YOU MUST ALREADY KNOW



- Hooks. The first 2 seconds d
 the whole video: first frame, opening line on screen, pattern interrupt.

- Retention pacing. No dead air, cuts that ride the voiceover, energy that builds instead of flatlines.

- Muted-first editing. Most feeds autoplay silent. Captions and graphics have to carry the video with the sound off.

- Caption craft. Emphasis on the words that carry the point, not random highlighting.

- The Hormozi style specifically: you have studied it, you have cut in it, and you know why it holds attention.



DELIVERABLES AND STANDARDS



- 9:16 as the primary deliverable, other ratios when we ask.

- MP4, H.264, captions burned in.

- Music and sound effects only from sources you hold rights to. Watermarked or unlicensed audio is an automatic reject, no exceptions.

- One revision pass included per video. We send notes in a single batch, you apply them once, done.

- Edit in whatever software you want. We judge output, not tools.



NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS



- Real, provable experience editing short-form content with serious motion graphics work, for creators, agencies, or businesses that had money riding on the videos.

- A real portfolio we can open: a reel, a site, or an organized Drive folder of your work. No portfolio, no consideration.

- You can take raw footage plus an outline and come back with something excellent, without a call, without twenty questions.

- Reliable on deadlines, every single time. We run content calendars. A late video is a missed slot. One missed deadline without warning ends the engagement.

- Attention to detail, because a misspelled caption or an off-beat graphic reads amateur instantly.

- Responsive on WhatsApp or Messenger during agreed hours, with honest ETAs. "It will be late, here is when" is acceptable. Silence is not.

- You take notes without ego and apply them precisely.



DO NOT APPLY IF



- You are a beginner or still learning the basics. This is not a starter role.

- Your motion graphics come from AI generators or untouched template packs.

- You want a one-off gig instead of a seat on a team.

- You need every cut dictated to you.

- Your portfolio has no caption-heavy, graphics-driven work in it.

- You juggle so many clients that 48-hour turnarounds scare you.



BONUS POINTS



- You have cut for business, marketing, or money channels in the Hormozi and Iman Gadzhi lane.

- Your sound design game is strong: whooshes, hits, and risers that make graphics feel physical.

- You have seen the performance data on your own edits and changed how you cut because of it.



PAY AND GROWTH



$30 per finished video, and the rate is negotiable up on quality: show us you cut at the level we are looking for and we pay for it. Work comes in batches as we need it, not on a fixed schedule. The goal is one editor who owns the MSET look long term. Paid through Wise, on time, every time.



HOW TO APPLY



Reply with the word CUTS as your first line. Then: a link to your full portfolio (reel, site, or organized Drive folder), links to 3 shorts you personally edited with your strongest motion graphics work in them, and one sentence on which of the 3 you would redo today and why. We check applications against every instruction in this post, including ones not repeated in this section. Miss any of them and you get skipped unread.



NEXT STEP



Shortlisted editors get a paid $20 test edit: our footage, our outline, 48-hour turnaround. The test is the interview. Pass it and the real work starts.



ONE LAST THING



Put the word KEYFRAME in the title of your application. That is how we know you read the whole post. No KEYFRAME in the title, no reply.

title: Static Ad Graphic Designer - Meta Lead Gen Creatives (Long-Term Team Role)
description:
WHO WE ARE



MSET is a US marketing agency running paid lead generation for local service businesses: contractors, roofers, remodelers, home services, and similar trades. Our static ads run on
 and Instagram with real money behind them, and they exist to do one thing: make a homeowner stop scrolling and fill out a form. Every design decision gets judged against that.



READ THIS FIRST



We are hiring a team member, not a gig worker. Someone we can rely on long term, who becomes part of how this agency operates and grows with it. This is not a beginner role: if you are new to design or have never made ads, do not apply. You will not pass the test and it will waste your time and ours.



One more thing. This post contains everything we require, and we do not take anyone seriously who applies without reading all of it. Your application will show us whether you did.



THE JOB



We send you the raw material: the copy, the offer, the claims, business info, and photos. You turn that into a finished static ad. That translation is the entire skill we are hiring: taking words and information and building the visual that makes them land.



And understand the bar here. Sometimes you get copy and nothing else. No reference, no mood board, no example to lean on. Blank canvas. We expect you to come back with something fire anyway, because the concept lives in your head, not in a swipe file. When we do hand you a reference, you match it or beat it. Both of these are the job. If only one of them is, this role is not for you.



THE STYLE RANGE (READ THIS TWICE)



This is the requirement we care about most. You must have a full arsenal, a real range of distinct design styles, and switch between them on command:



- Bold offer-led promos with big type and hard contrast

- Clean, premium, minimal layouts for high-ticket trust

- Busy retail-style price-and-deal designs

- Informational and editorial layouts that teach before they sell

- Before-and-after and proof-driven layouts

- Testimonial and review-card designs

- Native-feeling designs that do not read as ads at first glance



If every piece in your portfolio looks like the same designer made it on the same day, do not apply. One aesthetic is a dealbreaker here, no matter how good it is.



MARKETING KNOWLEDGE WE EXPECT



- Visual hierarchy as a selling tool: where the eye lands first, second, third, and why that order is hook, proof, offer.

- Thumb-stop thinking: what makes a static interrupt a feed scroll on a phone screen.

- The informational versus visual trade: when an ad should educate with density and when it should punch with one image and five words.

- Mobile-first legibility: type sizes, contrast, and safe zones that survive every Meta placement.

- Enough Meta ad policy awareness to design compliant: no misleading before-afters, no unreadable text walls.



DELIVERABLES AND STANDARDS



- Sizes per brief: 4:5 and 1:1 standard, 9:16 when asked.

- Layered source files delivered with every final (PSD, Figma, or equivalent). We own the working files.

- Fonts and stock imagery only from sources you hold rights to use commercially.

- You design with the claims, numbers, and reviews we give you. Never invent stats, testimonials, or guarantees. One fabricated element ends the engagement.

- One revision pass included per design. We send notes in a single batch, you apply them once, done.



NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS



- Real, provable experience designing lead generation ad creatives. Not just logos, not just branding decks, not just social posts.

- A real portfolio we can open: a site, a Behance, or an organized Drive folder, and it must show RANGE across different styles, not one look repeated.

- You can take copy and business information and come back with a strong visual from a blank canvas, no reference required, without a call, without twenty questions. Given a reference, you match it or beat it.

- Reliable on deadlines, every single time. A late creative is a missed launch. One missed deadline without warning ends the engagement.

- Speed. When we need a creative fast, you can turn a finished static in a couple of hours to a day, not in a week. Fast never excuses sloppy, and sloppy never excuses slow.

- Attention to detail, because one typo in a headline burns the whole ad spend behind it.

- Responsive on WhatsApp or Messenger during agreed hours, with honest ETAs. "It will be late, here is when" is acceptable. Silence is not.

- You take notes without ego and apply them precisely.



DO NOT APPLY IF



- You are a beginner or still building your fundamentals. This is not a starter role.

- You need a reference, a template, or an example ad before you can start designing.

- You have never designed an ad that actually ran with money behind it.

- You have one style you apply to everything.

- A same-day turnaround request would break your schedule.

- You want a one-off gig instead of a seat on a team.

- Your portfolio is illustration, logos, or branding with no ad work in it.

- You need every layout described to you before you can start.



BONUS POINTS



- You have designed for contractors, roofers, remodelers, cleaners, or other home services.

- You have seen performance data on your own ads and changed how you design because of it.

- You can flag weak copy when you see it and suggest the stronger line.



PAY AND GROWTH



$10 per finished static ad, and the rate is negotiable up on quality: show us you design at the level we are looking for and we pay for it. Work comes in batches as we need it, not on a fixed schedule. The goal is one designer who owns the MSET static look long term. Paid through Wise, on time, every time.



HOW TO APPLY



Reply with the word CONTRAST as your first line. Then: a link to your full portfolio, links or attachments for 3 static ads you personally designed that actually ran for real businesses (say so plainly if any were spec), and one sentence on which of the 3 you would redesign today and why. Pick 3 that prove your range, because three ads in the same style answers our biggest question the wrong way. We check applications against every instruction in this post, including ones not repeated in this section. Miss any of them and you get skipped unread.



NEXT STEP



Shortlisted designers get a paid $10 test: our copy and photos, one finished static, 48-hour turnaround. The test is the interview. Pass it and the real work starts.



ONE LAST THING



Put the word KERNING in the title of your application. That is how we know you read the whole post. No KERNING in the title, no reply.

title: Supply chain manager
description:
Supply Chain Manager (Part-Time) — Dropshipping E-Commerce

Type: Part-time (contract or employed)

About us

 We run a dropshipping model, sourcing products from international suppliers and localizing them into polished, US-ready listings. As we scale our product catalog and ad-driven sales, we need someone to bring structure and reliability to our supply chain.

The role

We're looking for a part-time Supply Chain Manager to own the flow of products from supplier to customer. You'll manage supplier relationships, keep sourcing costs and lead times under control, and make sure our fulfillment stays smooth as order volume grows. This is a hands-on, operational role with room to shape our processes from the ground up.

What you'll do



Manage relationships with international suppliers (Europe and Asia, including French and Chinese partners) and negotiate pricing, terms, and lead times

Monitor and optimize cost of goods (COG), shipping costs, and per-unit margins across product collections

Track inventory availability and supplier reliability to prevent stockouts and fulfillment delays

Vet and onboard new suppliers as we expand the catalog

Oversee order fulfillment and shipping performance, and resolve delivery or quality issues

Build and maintain simple, repeatable processes and reporting for sourcing and fulfillment

Work closely with the founder on product selection and margin planning



What you bring



Experience in supply chain, sourcing, procurement, or operations and especially fashion dropshipping

Familiarity with international supplier management and cross-border shipping to the US

Strong grasp of unit economics: COG, shipping, transaction costs, and margins

Comfort working with spreadsheets and e-commerce platforms (Shopify a plus)

Self-directed and reliable — you can own a domain without daily oversight

Clear communicator in English; additional languages (Chinese a bonus_



Must



Direct (fashion) dropshipping experience

Experience with Ai tools, slack, supplier platforms.

title: Meta Ads Manager Specialist — Daily Ad Uploads (Hourly, Long-Term)
description:
About us: US supplement brand (DTC + Amazon). Our creative team produces new video and static ads every single day. We need one person who gets them into Meta Ads Manager correctly, every day, without being told twice.



The role: You receive finished creatives and copy from our team and build them as ads inside our existing campaigns and ad sets. Naming convention, settings, links, placements — exactly as specified. This is pure execution. No media buying, no strategy, no budget or targeting decisions.



This role is for you if:



You have built hundreds of ads in Meta Ads Manager yourself and know every setting on the ad level without looking it up (Advantage+ creative toggles, placements, aspect ratio per placement, URL parameters, pixel, identity/page selection, standard vs. flexible ads)

You work from a brief without needing a call. You read, you build, you report.

You catch your own mistakes before we do



This role is NOT for you if:



You've only "assisted" someone who used Ads Manager

You'd need training on the Ads Manager interface itself

You need daily check-ins to feel confident



What you will do daily:



Build 10–30 new ads from our creative/copy handoff (Google Drive + copy doc)

Name every ad exactly by our convention

Run our launch checklist (URL, pixel, placements, ratios, creative enhancements off)

Update the tracker, flag broken or missing files in one message — no back-and-forth

Post a short daily completion report in 



Requirements:



3+ years hands-on inside Meta Ads Manager (not Meta Business Suite, not boosting posts)

Experience with e-commerce / DTC ad accounts

Zero-error mindset — one wrong link or setting costs real money

Good written English

Available every day (6 days/week), uploads completed by 9:00 AM CET

Own computer, stable internet



Pay & setup:



$7/hour, paid weekly, tracked hours

Roughly 2–3 hours per day to start, more as volume grows

SOP + Loom for our specific setup on day one. After that, you're expected to run it.



How to apply: Start your application with the word RHODIOLA. Then answer in 5 sentences max:



How many ads have you personally built in Ads Manager? Which accounts/niches?

In a standard (non-flexible) video ad, list the settings you check before publishing.

Your available hours in CET.



Applications without RHODIOLA or with generic copy-paste answers are not read.

title: AI Digital Content Creator – Cinematic Video & Photography
description:

This is not a traditional graphic design role.



We want someone who is passionate about AI and knows how to use the latest generative AI tools to create realistic photography, cinematic video, advertising creatives and social media content that looks professionally produced.



What You'll Be Creating



You’ll work across different brands and industries to create:



Cinematic AI-generated videos

Realistic AI photography and product photography

Short-form video content for Instagram, TikTok and YouTube

AI-generated adverts and promotional videos

Product and lifestyle visuals

Brand campaigns and storytelling content

Talking characters / AI avatars where required

Image-to-video content

Creative concepts for client campaigns

High-quality social media visuals



The goal is to create content that makes people ask:



“How did they make that?”



AI Tools



We’re interested in candidates who have experience with tools such as:



Kling AI

Runway

Veo

Midjourney

Flux

Nano Banana / Gemini

Higgsfield

HeyGen

ElevenLabs

ChatGPT

Adobe Photoshop

CapCut / Premiere Pro / DaVinci Resolve



You do not need to know every tool listed above.



More importantly, you should understand prompting, composition, lighting, camera movement, consistency, storytelling and editing.



We also want someone who actively keeps up with new AI tools and techniques as the industry develops.



What We're Looking For



You should have:



Strong experience creating AI-generated images and/or video

A portfolio showing your best AI creative work

Excellent visual taste

Understanding of cinematic lighting and composition

Ability to create realistic and consistent characters/products

Strong prompting skills

Video editing experience

Ability to take a basic idea and turn it into a finished creative

Attention to detail

Good written English

Ability to work independently and meet deadlines

A genuine interest in AI and emerging creative technology



Your portfolio is more important to us than qualifications.



What Would Make You Stand Out



We're particularly interested if you can create content that looks like it was produced using a real camera, professional lighting and a full production team.



Experience creating AI content for:



Brands

Restaurants

Property

Automotive

Health & fitness

Clinics

Products

Social media advertising



would also be a big advantage.



About the Role



You'll be working remotely with our team on a variety of projects.

title: Video Ad Editor - Meta Lead Gen Creatives (Long-Term Team Role)
description:
WHO WE ARE



MSET is a US marketing agency running paid lead generation for local service businesses: contractors, roofers, remodelers, home services, and similar trades. Our ads run on
 and Instagram, and they exist to do exactly one thing: make a homeowner stop scrolling and fill out a form. Every editing decision gets judged against that. Views mean nothing to us. Leads are the scoreboard.



READ THIS FIRST



We are hiring a team member, not a gig worker. Someone we can rely on every single week, long term, who becomes part of how this agency operates and grows with it. The per-video pay is how we start, not what this is. And this is not a beginner role: if you are new to editing or new to ads, do not apply. You will not pass the test and it will waste your time and ours.



One more thing. This post contains everything we require, and we do not take anyone seriously who applies without reading all of it. Your application will show us whether you did.



THE JOB



You edit our ad creatives. We send you raw footage (real job sites, real crews, real talking-head takes) plus a written outline: the hook, the angle, the offer, the CTA. You turn that into a finished, high-performing ad that could go live the same day. The outline tells you what the ad says. You d
 how it hits: pacing, caption emphasis, b-roll choices, sound design, where the cut lands. That judgment is what we are paying for.



WHAT WE MEAN WHEN WE SAY YOU MUST KNOW MARKETING



This is the part most applicants fail, so read it carefully. We are not hiring a technical editor who waits to be told where to cut. You need to already understand, from experience:



- Hooks. Why the first 2 seconds d
 the whole ad. First-frame choice, opening line on screen, visual pattern interrupts, and how a hook changes when the audience is a homeowner with a problem versus a bored scroller.

- Retention. Scene changes every 2 to 3 seconds, no dead air, cuts that ride the voiceover, caption emphasis on the words that carry the claim.

- Muted-first editing. Most of Meta autoplays silent. If your ad needs audio to work, it does not work.

- Direct-response structure. Problem, agitation, proof, offer, CTA, and how to compress that into 30 seconds without it feeling rushed.

- The formats that win in lead gen, and when each one fits: owner talking direct to camera, job-site walkthroughs, before/after transformations, testimonial cuts, UGC-style phone footage, offer-led ads, VSL-style longer cuts.

- The offer. Why the hook and the offer have to match, and why a beautiful ad with a buried offer loses to an ugly ad with a clear one.



If you read that list and it felt like your day job, keep reading. If it felt like a course syllabus, stop here.



AI GENERATION SKILLS (TELL US IF YOU HAVE THIS)



We also want editors who have used AI video generation to assist an edit: Higgsfield especially, or similar tools, plus the prompt-writing skill to get usable output. To be clear about the role AI plays here: our ads are cut from real footage, and AI generation fills gaps: a b-roll shot we could not film, a transition, an accent element. You are never generating a whole ad from a prompt, and an application built on fully AI-made videos will not pass. If you have used AI this way, say so in your application and show an example.



DELIVERABLES AND STANDARDS



- Every ad delivered in both 9:16 and 4:5.

- MP4, H.264, captions burned in, safe margins respected for every Meta placement.

- Music and sound effects only from sources you hold rights to. Watermarked or unlicensed audio is an automatic reject and ends the test, no exceptions, because it puts ad accounts at risk.

- One revision pass included per video. We send notes in a single batch, you apply them once, done.

- Edit in whatever software you want. We judge output, not tools.



NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS



- Real, provable experience editing ad creatives or short-form content for lead gen or local service businesses. Not music videos, not gaming content, not wedding films.

- A real portfolio we can open: a reel, a site, or an organized Drive folder of your work. No portfolio, no consideration.

- You can take a folder of raw clips plus a one-page outline and come back with something high-performing, without a call, without twenty questions.

- Reliable on deadlines, every single time. We run ad calendars. A late video is a missed launch. One missed deadline without warning ends the engagement.

- Attention to detail, because a wrong caption or a missed spec burns ad spend.

- Responsive on WhatsApp or Messenger during agreed hours, with honest ETAs. "It will be late, here is when" is acceptable. Silence is not.

- You take notes without ego and apply them precisely.



DO NOT APPLY IF



- You are a beginner or still learning the basics. This is not a starter role.

- You have never edited an ad that actually ran with money behind it.

- You want a one-off gig instead of a seat on a team.

- You need every cut dictated to you.

- Your portfolio is cinematic montages with no captions and no CTA.

title: CINEMATIC FACELESS BIBLE YOUTUBE CHANNEL
description:
# VIDEO EDITOR NEEDED — CINEMATIC FACELESS BIBLE YOUTUBE CHANNEL



We are launching a new faceless YouTube channel focused on **cinematic biblical stories, mysteries, supernatural events and historical storytelling**.



We are looking for a **long-term video editor** who can turn scripts + voiceovers + visual references into engaging, cinematic YouTube videos.



This is NOT a generic slideshow channel.



We want the videos to feel like **documentaries / cinematic historical films**, with strong storytelling, atmosphere, pacing and sound design.



## WHAT YOU WILL RECEIVE



For each video, we will provide:



* Finished script

* Voiceover

* Channel visual identity

* Visual references

* AI image/video prompts when needed

* Editing guidelines

* Music/SFX references



Your job is to transform these assets into a polished final YouTube video.



## VIDEO STYLE



Think:



* Cinematic biblical documentaries

* Historical storytelling

* Dark / mysterious atmosphere

* Epic environments

* Dramatic battles

* Ancient civilizations

* Supernatural biblical events

* Strong visual storytelling

* Professional sound design



The channel will cover stories such as:



* Noah and the Flood

* The Nephilim

* Sodom and Gomorrah

* Moses and the Exodus

* David and Goliath

* Daniel

* Angels and biblical mysteries

* Prophecies

* Revelation / Apocalypse



## VIDEO LENGTH



Initial test:



**5–8 minutes**



Long-term videos:



**20–40 minutes**



Potentially longer as the channel grows.



## YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES



You will:



* Edit the voiceover into a compelling visual story

* Select and/or create appropriate visuals

* Use stock footage, AI visuals and provided assets

* Synchronize visuals with narration

* Create cinematic pacing

* Add music

* Add sound effects

* Add atmospheric effects

* Use subtle motion/animation on still images when appropriate

* Create transitions that feel natural

* Maintain visual continuity between scenes

* Deliver a clean 16:9 YouTube master



## IMPORTANT



We DO NOT want:



* Generic AI slideshow videos

* Random stock footage

* Repetitive zoom-in/zoom-out effects

* Excessive transitions

* Cheap-looking templates

* Visuals that do not match the narration

* Videos that feel mass-produced



We want:



**STORY → EMOTION → ATMOSPHERE → RETENTION**



The viewer should feel like they are watching a biblical cinematic documentary.



## SOFTWARE



You can use:



* Adobe Premiere Pro

* DaVinci Resolve

* After Effects

* CapCut

* Photoshop

* AI video/image tools



We don't care which software you use as long as the final result is excellent.



Experience with AI tools such as Runway, Kling, Veo, Midjourney, Flux, Leonardo, Higgsfield, etc. is a major advantage.



## THE TEST



Before starting a long-term collaboration, we will select several candidates for a **paid 5–8 minute test edit**.



Everyone will receive the same:



* Script

* Voiceover

* Visual references

* Brand style

* Instructions



This allows us to compare editing quality fairly.



We are looking for the editor who can create the strongest final result — NOT simply the cheapest editor.



## WHAT WE CARE ABOUT MOST



1. Storytelling

2. Visual quality

3. Pacing / retention

4. Sound design

5. Biblical atmosphere

6. Attention to detail

7. Reliability

8. Communication

9. Ability to follow a production system

10. Price



## LONG-TERM OPPORTUNITY



If the test is successful, this can become a **long-term recurring position**.



We plan to increase production as the channel grows.



The ideal editor will eventually work with us on a consistent weekly production schedule.



## TO APPLY



Please send:



1. Your country

2. Your hourly rate

3. Your price for a 10-minute video

4. Your price for a 20-minute video

5. Your price for a 30-minute video

6. Your usual turnaround time

7. Your editing software

8. Your experience with faceless YouTube

9. Your experience with documentaries/history/religious content

10. Your experience with AI-generated visuals

11. Your portfolio

12. ONE example of your best long-form documentary/faceless edit



### IMPORTANT APPLICATION TEST



Start your application with:



**"BIBLE CINEMATIC — I READ EVERYTHING"**



Applications without this phrase will not be considered.



We are looking for someone who wants to build something long-term, not just complete one video.

title: Cold Caller / Appointment Setter — US Small Business (Barbershops, Texas) — Night Shift
description:
ABOUT DJM INNOVATIONS

DJM Innovations is a software company based in the Dallas-Fort Worth

area of Texas, United States. We build and manage custom booking and

scheduling systems for American small businesses - owner-operated

companies that are currently renting generic software they don't like

and don't own. We build them a system that's actually theirs, and we

support it for them long-term.



We are a small, growing team. This is a real, ongoing role on that

team - not a one-off project, not a trial gig. We are hiring one

person and we intend to keep them.



THE ROLE

Outbound Appointment Setter. You call small business owners in Texas

and book 15-minute Google Meet consultations for our founder.



You are the first voice these owners hear from our company. The

quality of that conversation determines whether we get in the room.

This is the most important seat in our sales process.



CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

- Make outbound calls to a pre-built, pre-qualified list (you will

  never have to source your own leads)

- Reach the business owner or decision maker

- Explain what we do clearly and briefly, in your own words - we will

  train you on this and you'll have it in front of you

- Qualify the business against a short checklist

- Book a specific date and time for a 15-minute Google Meet

- Send the calendar invite, a confirmation message, and a same-morning

  reminder for every booked call

- Maintain accurate call records in our shared tracker

- Work a monthly follow-up cycle on "not right now" leads

- Rebook no-shows



WHERE YOUR ROLE ENDS

You are not a closer, and we will never ask you to be one. The

following always go to the founder:

- Pricing, in any form

- Detailed technical questions

- Contracts, timelines, and guarantees

- Serious objections from an interested buyer



Your line: "That's exactly what the call is for - he's the one who

builds these and he'll walk you through it properly. Are you better

Tuesday morning or Wednesday?"



SCHEDULE

Monday to Friday, 10:00 PM - 2:00 AM Philippine Standard Time.

This aligns with late morning in Texas, which is when these owners

answer their phones.



20 hours per week to start. This is a permanent night shift - please

do not apply unless you can hold this schedule consistently.



COMPENSATION AND TERMS

- Salary as listed above, paid twice monthly, on time, every time

- Paid one-week trial period before any long-term commitment on

  either side

- Performance review at 90 days. If you hit target, the role moves to

  full time at an increased rate, plus a bonus on every appointment

  that converts to a signed client

- Philippine public holidays observed

- Paid time off after 6 months

- Written agreement provided before you start - you will know exactly

  what you're agreeing to



WHAT WE PROVIDE

- A dialer and a US phone number - you use no personal minutes

- A tested call framework and recorded example calls before your first

  live dial

- The full prospect list, built and maintained for you

- Weekly one-on-one coaching from the founder, reviewing your own

  recorded calls

- Direct access to the founder. There is no manager layer between us.



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required:

- Clear, neutral, confident spoken English. This carries more weight

  than everything else on this list combined.

- The ability to sound like a person, not a script. Our buyers are

  blue-collar American owners who are working while you call them.

- Resilience. Most calls end in a no. That is the job, not a problem

  with the job.

- Stable, reliable internet and a quiet, dedicated workspace

- Consistency. Someone dependable at 80% is worth far more to us than

  someone brilliant who disappears.



Preferred:

- Prior US outbound B2B calling or BPO experience

- Familiarity with any dialer, CRM, or Google Calendar workflow

- Experience calling small businesses rather than consumers



HOW TO APPLY

We review every complete application. Incomplete applications are not

reviewed.



1. Begin your message with the word TEXAS, so we know you've read

   this posting in full.



2. Send a link to a short voice recording (Vocaroo, Google Drive, or

   any file-sharing link). Please do not read a script.



   In under 45 seconds: imagine you have just called a small business,

   the owner has picked up, and he sounds busy. Open the call in your

   own words and try to earn a 15-minute video call. Use any industry

   you like - we are assessing how you sound and how you think, not

   what you say.



3. Answer briefly, one or two sentences each:

   a) The owner says "we're fine, we don't need it" and starts to end

      the call. What do you do?

   b) Ninety seconds in, the owner asks "how much does this cost?"

      What do you say?



Shortlisted applicants will be invited to a paid one-week trial.



Thank you for reading this far. We know what it's like to be on the

other side of a job board, and we take applications seriously.

title: EXPERT MEDIA BUYER — META & GOOGLE ADS
description:
SENIOR MEDIA BUYER — META & GOOGLE ADS (ECOM / DTC)



We’re looking for a Senior Media Buyer who can do both: launch DTC brands from zero and scale them to 10k/day, and also manage and optimize accounts already running high-spend volumes. This is not an entry-level or “boost the post” role. We operate multiple DTC brands across several markets, with serious budgets and high creative output.



Fair warning before you apply: knowing how to run Meta and Google ads is not enough. If you don’t actually understand our methodology, don’t apply. You’ll be tested on it during screening and filtered out fast, so let’s not waste each other’s time.



You’ll work directly with our EU team.



Who we’re looking for



On Meta: you need know creative is the main lever. The algorithm finds the audience, you feed it clean signal and strong creative.



On Google: you need know the Feed is your targeting. You don’t win with endless keyword lists, you win by structuring the feed to feed the AI.



You need read an account top-down: offer > creative/feed > landing page > account. You consolidate data, you don’t hyper-segment.



Responsibilities



 1. Own the launch of new DTC brands from $0 to $10k/day revenue on Meta + Google

 2. Meta: ABO testing > CBO scaling > MOF/BOF/Retargeting, broad-led, Advantage+

 3. Google: own GMC feed optimization, Shopping and PMax, structuring titles and attributes to feed Google’s AI

 4. Manage and optimize already-scaled, high-spend accounts without breaking performance

 5. Build architectures that consolidate signal, not fragment it

 6. Work hand-in-hand with Creative Strategists, 30+ creatives/week

 7. Diagnose underperformance by layer, not by reflex

 8. Manage real budgets with discipline and P&L reporting



Requirements



META:



 • Proven track record launching AND scaling DTC brands, at least one brand taken from zero to 5-10k/day and 100k+/month managed



GOOGLE — THIS IS CRITICAL:



 • Feed Optimization (GMC): you know that in today’s Google, feed optimization IS your targeting, not an afterthought

 • Consolidation & Scale Architecture: you know consolidation beats hyper-segmentation, and you know when to use Standard Shopping vs Performance Max depending on the stage of the launch



General:



 • Strong on direct-response and unit economics, AOV, CPA, payback, contribution

 • Fluent English, EU timezone overlap



What we offer



 • Remote, long-term, you launch from scratch and also manage mature accounts

 • Direct work with founders + dedicated creative team

 • Serious budgets to scale



To Apply



Send:



 • Brief intro

 • Track record: 1-2 brands you took from zero to scale with real numbers, day 0 spend, time to 10k/day, peak daily spend, ROAS, both Meta and Google



Screening questions



 1. How many brands have you personally taken from $0 to $10k/day? Walk me through one.

 2. What’s the largest daily spend you’ve personally managed on Meta and on Google while keeping it profitable? For how long?

 3. Walk me through your framework to go from $0 to $10k/day with a new DTC product on Meta + Google. Phases, budgets, kill/scale rules.

 4. You inherit an account already spending a high daily budget. How do you diagnose whether to keep scaling or stabilize? What do you check first?

 5. How do you optimize a Shopping feed title? Where exactly do you place the main keyword, attributes and brand? Give me a before/after example.

 6. Standard Shopping vs PMax, when do you switch, and what data do you need?

 7. You get 15+ new creatives per week. How do you test them without resetting learning on your scaling CBO?

 8. Tell me about a launch that failed from zero, Meta or Google, and what you learned.

Excessive transitions



Meme overload

title: VIDEO EDITOR — LONG-TERM PARTNERSHIP
description:
???? VIDEO EDITOR — LONG-TERM PARTNERSHIP | $8 PER REEL



I'm looking for a reliable video editor to work with long-term.



I run an online fitness coaching business for men 300lbs+ and regularly create short-form content and ads for Instagram,
 and other platforms: 



I'm NOT looking for someone to work 40 hours a week.



I'm looking for an editing partner I can keep on standby and message whenever I have content that needs editing.



Sometimes I'll need 1 video edited.

Sometimes I'll send you 5–20 videos at once.

Other times there may be nothing for a few days.



The important thing is that when I send you an edit, you're reliable, responsive and can get it done quickly.



???? PAY

$8 USD per reel

- Videos are typically 1–2 minutes maximum.

- I'm looking for someone I can build a long-term relationship with, not someone for a one-off project.



???? THE STYLE I'M LOOKING FOR



I want someone who can create high-retention, modern short-form videos and ads similar to the style/content on:

DFitz Academy: 

Biology Decoded: 

Instagram reference: 



The editing should feel:

• Fast-paced

• Clean

• Professional

• Premium

• High-retention

• Attention-grabbing

• Native to Instagram/Reels

• Not overly flashy or cheesy

• Strong subtitles/captions

• Good pacing and cuts

• Strategic zooms/punch-ins

• B-roll when appropriate

• Visual emphasis on important words/points

• Designed to keep someone watching



I do NOT want generic CapCut-style edits with random effects thrown everywhere.

I want someone who understands why an edit works, not someone who simply knows how to cut clips together.



???? AUDIO QUALITY — BIG BONUS



Bonus points if you're genuinely good at audio editing.

I want the final videos to sound clean, crisp and professional.



Things like:

• Removing background noise

• Improving voice clarity

• Balancing audio levels

• Cleaning up echo/room noise

• Making speech sound more professional

• Adding subtle sound effects when appropriate

• Making sure music/B-roll doesn't overpower the voice



You don't need to be a professional audio engineer.



But if you know how to take average raw audio and make it sound significantly better, that's a BIG plus.

Basically:

Don't just make the video look good — make it sound good too.



???? ENGLISH IS IMPORTANT

You must have good English.

A big part of the job involves creating accurate subtitles, so you need to be able to understand what I'm saying and correctly subtitle the videos.

You'll need to have:

• Good English comprehension

• Good spelling and grammar

• Accurate subtitle/captioning skills

• Good attention to detail

• Clear communication



If your English is poor, please don't apply.



⚡ RELIABILITY IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT

This is probably the most important part of the job.

I don't need you available 24/7.

But when I message you:

"Hey, I've got 3 videos for you."

I need to know that you'll actually respond and get them done.



I'm looking for someone who:

• Responds reasonably quickly

• Meets deadlines

• Doesn't disappear

• Takes initiative

• Can work independently

• Pays attention to detail

• Is open to feedback

• Can follow instructions

• Wants to build a long-term working relationship



Initially, I'll give you examples and feedback so you understand exactly how I want the videos edited.



Once you understand my style, I want you to be able to take a raw video and run with it.



???? WHAT YOU'LL RECEIVE

I'll generally provide:

• Raw video footage

• The topic/script/context

• Examples of the editing style

• Any specific instructions



You handle the editing and deliver the finished reel.



I'm not expecting you to be available all day.



I just need to know that when I send work through, you can communicate with me and get it done.



⭐ WHO I'M LOOKING FOR

You'd be a great fit if you're:

• Experienced with short-form content

• Comfortable editing talking-head videos

• Experienced with Instagram Reels

• Good at editing ads

• Very good at subtitles/captions

• Good with pacing and retention

• Good with audio cleanup

• Detail-oriented

• Fast without sacrificing quality

• Fluent in English

• Reliable and responsive

• Comfortable receiving feedback

• Able to work independently

• Looking for a long-term client



???? PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING

I'm not looking for someone who just wants another job where they clock in and clock out.



I'm looking for a video editing partner I can rely on.



If we work well together, there can be regular batches of content and ongoing work for the long term.



I'm much more interested in finding one excellent editor I can trust than constantly hiring different freelancers.



???? HOW TO APPLY

Please send me the following:

1. Your portfolio

Send your best short-form video examples.

Talking-head videos, fitness content, ads, direct-response content or similar styles are especially relevant.

2. Your experience

If I send you a 1–2 minute raw video, how quickly can you normally return the finished edit?

I'm looking for someone who understands editing for retention, not just someone who knows how to use editing software.



I'm looking for someone I can work with long-term, so take a little time with your application and show me what you can do.

title: Compliance & Document Assistant — US Homecare (Part-Time, Long-Term)
description:
WHO WE ARE



We help small home care agencies in the Midwest stay compliant with state healthcare regulations. Most of these agencies are run by one to three people who are excellent at caring for clients and overwhelmed by the office Work. If they miss a signature, an expired document, or a required training record, they can lose their license. We are the back office that makes sure that never happens while saving them on hours and costs. 



The company is run by a former home care agency owner who grew a previous agency to over 90 members before starting this business. You will work directly with the owner, not through layers of management.



THE ROLE



This is a long-term, part-time position, not a short project and not a one-off gig. It start at around 20-25 hours per week. We are adding new agency clients on an ongoing basis, and this seat is expected to grow into full-time work as that happens. You are one of the first hires, and the role will grow with you.



This is heavy document production work. You will be formatting e-signature templates, prefilling forms, organizing client files, and building/revising checklists. It is detailed, sometimes repetitive, and unforgiving of sloppiness. If you want variety and creativity from day one, this is not the role.



What makes it interesting is what comes after. As you learn the regulations, you take over more of the thinking work: reading a rule, d
 what documents it requires, and building the system that produces them. You will write the SOPs for your own job as you go, to help these struggling Home care agencies. 



WHAT YOU WILL DO



- Build and format document templates in BoldSign (very similar to DocuSign): field placement, signer roles, naming conventions

- Prefill and prepare client and employee compliance documents from source files

- Organize and audit client and employee files in Dropbox against a compliance checklist

- Read state licensing rules from Department Human services for example provided to you, and learn how the system works

- Track expiring items: background checks, trainings, service agreements, certifications etc.

- Write and maintain the SOP for every process you touch

- Some claims and billing reviewing in a EHR system to make sure the agency is up to date.



WHAT YOU WILL NOT DO



- No client contact. No client calls/emails. Everything routes through the owner.

- No sales, no lead generation, no social media, no cold outreach.



SCHEDULE



- 20-25 hours per week, Monday to Friday, with room to grow into full-time if desired

- Hours are flexible within reason, but the role requires overlap with US Central Time business hours (roughly 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM CDT). In Philippine time, that window is late night into early morning. Please be realistic about what you can sustain long-term.

- You may keep other clients, but not during your committed hours. 

- $300 - $500 USD per month, depending on experience

- Paid twice per month

- Pay increases as you get faster, need less oversight, and take on more responsibilities, and increases again as hours grow toward full-time. This is not a vague promise; it is how the role is designed. Additional benefits are discussed after probation period.



WHO I AM ACTUALLY LOOKING FOR



No prior knowledge of specific US or Midwest healthcare regulation is required. I provide the source material and the detail. Most applicants have little to not experience with a state licensing rule, and that is fine.



What I cannot train is this: I need someone who can be handed a regulation they have never seen and come back with a working checklist and a list of smart questions, without being walked through it step by step.



Beyond that, I am looking for someone genuinely curious. This role has autonomy, and autonomy only works if you use it. That means:



- Asking questions when something does not make sense, instead of guessing or stalling

- Noticing when a process is inefficient and telling me, rather than doing it the slow way forever

- Bringing ideas and suggestions, not just completed tasks

- Learning on your own between tasks instead of waiting for the next instruction 



If you need every step explained twice, this will not work. If you enjoy taking something confusing and making it orderly, you will do well here.



You also need:



- Excellent written English. You will write checklists and SOPs that will be relied on.

- Genuine attention to detail. One missing signature is a real problem for a real business.

- Reliability. If you say something is done, it is done and it is correct.



BACKGROUNDS THAT TRANSLATE WELL



Paralegal, audit, quality assurance, healthcare administration, medical billing, insurance, accounting, public health, or any office admin role where you managed compliance documents or licensing paperwork.



Helpful but not mandatory: BoldSign, DocuSign, PandaDoc, JotForm, Google Workspace, Dropbox, Notion, any US EHR system, or previous work supporting a US home care or home health agency.



CONFIDENTIALITY



You will handle protected health information covered by US HIPAA regulations, and you will be required to sign a confidentiality agreement. This means a private, secure workspace, not a shared computer and not a public network.



GROWTH



We are adding new agency clients on an ongoing basis, and this seat is the foundation of the delivery team. The person in this role is expected to move into a senior position, owning processes, assisting new hires, and reviewing their work, as we grow. Hours and pay increase along the way.



HOW TO APPLY



Do not send a generic cover letter. Reply and answer all nine questions below, numbered, in the body of your application. Applications that skip questions will not be reviewed. Also Put the word "Compliance office assistant" in your subject line or application title



1. List the specific hours you can reliably work each weekday, stated in US Central Time. Reliable high-speed internet, a quiet space with no background noise for meetings, a good working computer, a good pair of headsets with a clear microphone is a required.



2. Describe the most complicated document, file, or process you have ever been responsible for organizing or cleaning up. What was messy about it, what did you do, and how did you know when it was right?



3. Have you ever had to read a policy, rule, contract, or manual and turn it into something usable, such as a checklist, template, summary, or process? Tell me what it was and how you approached it.



4. Tell me about a time you suggested a better way to do something at work, without being asked. What happened?



5. Which of these have you used, and how much: BoldSign, DocuSign, PandaDoc, JotForm, Google Workspace, Dropbox, Notion, any US EHR or billing system. 



6. Are you currently working with other clients? How many hours per week, and doing what?



7. What is your expected monthly rate for 20-25 hours per week?



8. Best contact method and number, plus your availability for an interview in the next 12-48 hours.



9. Paste a link to your audio or video introduction. This is required. It does not need to be polished, a phone recording is fine. Answer two things: tell me about yourself, and tell me about a time you had to learn something difficult on your own, without anyone to teach you. Use any tool you like Vocaroo, Google Drive, Loom, YouTube unlisted, or Dropbox. 



Your resume is optional. Your answers matter more.



First group of Interview requests go out starting within 6 to 12 hours of your application, so please make sure you list your preferred method of contact.

title: Earthworks Estimator - Grading, Cut and Fill Take-Off Specialist
description:
Full-time | Monday to Friday, Australian business hours | Long-term | Above market pay



ABOUT THE ROLE



This is a full-time role with an established Victorian civil construction contractor. Their work is earthworks, drainage and pavements on subcontract civil packages to head builders, on jobs between roughly AUD 200,000 and AUD 5 million.



Grading and earthworks take-off is the most important task in this role. Everything else sits behind it.



This is a specialist role. We are not looking for a general construction estimator. We are looking for someone whose core skill is earthworks and grading takeoff on civil projects.





BEFORE YOU APPLY, ANSWER THIS TO YOURSELF



On your last earthworks job, what bulking or shrinkage factor did you apply, and why that number? If that question does not have an immediate answer for you, this role is not for you.



Please do not apply if your estimating background is buildings, fit-out, MEP, structural steel or general trade packages. Please do not apply if your earthworks experience is checking or pricing quantities that somebody else measured.





WHAT YOU WOULD DO



- Build cut and fill take-offs from civil drawings

- Measure pavements and stormwater drainage

- Work from geotechnical reports and structural drawings as well as the civil set

- Produce your own working, in a form someone else can audit

- Flag scope gaps, assumptions, exclusions and risk items before a number goes out

- Work to Australian terminology, units and standards





TOOLS AND SOFTWARE



You will be properly equipped. If you need a specific tool to do the work well, tell us in Question 8 and we will sort it out.



What we care about is whether you can build a surface from a drawing, produce a take-off you can stand behind, and know when a number looks wrong.





MUST HAVE



ESSENTIAL: A civil engineering or quantity surveying background, with real experience behind it.



ESSENTIAL: Grading and earthworks take-off experience on civil or infrastructure projects, on real jobs you can describe in detail.



ESSENTIAL: You can read a geotechnical report and price from it.



- Able to read civil drawings and structural drawings

- Experience measuring pavements and stormwater drainage

- Strong Excel

- Fluent in a PDF measurement and mark-up tool

- Excellent written and spoken English

- Available Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm Australian Eastern Time

- Reliable internet and a professional home working setup





NICE TO HAVE



- Australian project experience

- Bulk earthworks on subdivisions, land development or road projects

- Experience building surfaces from contours, spot levels or point files

- Experience pricing from first-principles rate libraries, including plant and labour rates





WORK SAMPLES - PLEASE READ THIS CAREFULLY



We are asking every applicant to attach examples of earthworks and grading take-off work you have actually done. This is the single biggest thing that will get your application looked at.



Send as many of these four as you can. One is better than none. All four will get your application read first.



1. A grading or earthworks take-off spreadsheet showing cut and fill

2. An earthworks heat map, or a cut and fill colour map

3. A pavement take-off mark-up

4. A drainage take-off mark-up



REDACT ANYTHING CONFIDENTIAL. 





WHAT IS ON OFFER



- Above market rate pay

- Full-time and long-term with one client, not project-by-project gig work

- Supported by a dedicated manager whose role is to help you succeed

- Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm Australian Eastern Time. (with some variations by agreement)

- Ongoing salary reviews





HOW TO APPLY



Submit your updated resume, attach your work samples, and answer every question below.



ATTENTION: you must directly answer these questions in your application to be considered. Applications without answers will not be read.





1. List the files you have attached and what each one is. If you have attached nothing, write NONE.



2. Name two earthworks jobs you took off. For each one: the project type, the approximate cut and fill volumes, whether the site balanced, and what you did with the surplus or the shortfall.



3. A car park levels plan gives you finished surface levels. The pavement build-up is 40mm asphalt on 100mm Class 3 on 200mm Class 4. Landscape areas get 100mm of topsoil. You have already built the existing surface from the feature survey. What surface do you difference against to get the bulk earthworks cut and fill, and how do you build it?



4. Show your arithmetic on this one. Cut is 8,000 cubic metres and fill is 8,000 cubic metres, measured between surfaces. The geotechnical report gives a bulking factor of 25% and a compaction factor of 10% for the site clay. Does the site balance? What do you order in, and what do you cart away?



5. A geotechnical report tells you: uncontrolled fill to 0.8m, stiff clay below, groundwater at 2.6m, refusal at 3.2m, and rock in one borehole only at 2.9m. The structural drawings show a basement pad requiring excavation to 1.5m across the footprint. What do you price differently because of that report, and what do you write as an exclusion or an assumption when the number goes out?



6. A 180m run of DN450 Class 3 concrete pipe falls from 1.2m to 4.1m of cover across five pits. How do you measure and structure this for pricing, and what quantities besides the pipe itself do you produce?



7. Which earthworks quantities end up in a contract but do not appear as a line or a level on the civil drawings? Where do you find them? If you have worked to Australian standards or specifications, name one and one thing it required that changed your quantities.



8. What software do you use, and what would you want us to provide? Say roughly how many years on each. If there is a tool you work best in that you do not currently have access to, name it.



9. What is your expected monthly salary in PHP, what hours do you work right now, and when could you start?
salary: Above market rates based on experience

title: Finance & Operations Coordinator — Remote (Day Shift)
description:
Finance & Operations Coordinator — Remote (Day Shift)



TYPE OF WORK: Bookkeeping, Finance, Operations

HOURS PER WEEK: 40

JOB CATEGORY: Finance & Accounting

EMPLOYMENT TYPE: Full-Time

SALARY: $1,200–$1,400/month



JOB DESCRIPTION



We are a leading U.S.-based communications firm serving mission-driven organizations — schools, healthcare organizations, nonprofits, advocacy groups, campaigns, and civic institutions. We help our clients build visibility, public trust, and real momentum through strategy, creative, advertising, and outreach. We also manage our own portfolio of properties that generate recurring revenue and fund our operations.



We run a lean, AI-enabled operation and are growing fast. We need a sharp Finance & Operations Coordinator to own the money side end to end — someone who manages client invoicing, subcontractor payments, vendor costs, and keeps the books current. You'll work directly with the founder on cash management and directly with vendors and customers. This is the financial operations backbone of a growing firm and multi-property real estate business with recurring client contracts and active freelance talent. One big project: in December, you'll catch up eight months of backlogged bookkeeping during the quieter month.



Schedule: Three daytime Philippine options: 4AM–1PM PHT, 6AM–3PM PHT, or 7AM–4PM PHT. You'll have a twice-weekly check-in with the founder in PT (typically brief, structured, 15–20 minutes).



WHAT YOU WILL DO



Client Invoicing & Receivables

- Implement contract-to-cash: watch for fully executed contracts, draft the first invoice, and send it immediately

- Create and send recurring monthly invoices to clients

- Track what's paid, what's outstanding, and when to follow up

- Enforce payment terms (typically: invoice on delivery, payment due in 30 days)

- Keep AR aging clean and flag slow payers



Subcontractor Payments & Communication

- Review freelancer and vendor invoices for accuracy and rate verification

- Compile invoices into payment batches

- Log payment history and match to contracts

- Communicate with subcontractors about invoice status and timing

- Flag rate anomalies or scope creep

- Confirm a completed W-9 is on file before approving any first-time contractor invoice

- Track which vendors/subcontractors are approaching the $
reporting threshold and flag for year-end 1099 prep



Vendor Cost Management

- Build and maintain a directory of vendors (contractors, service providers, tool subscriptions)

- Document cost per item or rate per hour

- Run a quarterly rate audit: confirm we're getting competitive pricing

- Flag subscriptions that should be cancelled or renegotiated

- Present vendor cost trends in weekly and monthly reporting



Bookkeeping & Monthly Close

- Reconcile bank accounts, credit cards, and payments (AP/AR)

- Categorize transactions into the chart of accounts

- Handle month-end reconciliation and close

- Use QuickBooks Online as your system of record

- December project: catch up eight months of backlogged entries and reconciliation



Cash Flow & Reporting

- Analyze cash flow weekly: money in, money out, runway, timing mismatches

- Prepare a weekly cash flow summary for the founder

- Monthly: produce a financial package (cash position, receivables aging, vendor summary, budget variance)

- Track and forecast based on contract pipeline and known expenses



Compliance Calendar

- Maintain a calendar of key annual deadlines (business registration renewals, 1099 filings, insurance renewals, and other regulatory dates)

- Set reminders at 60, 30, 14, and 7 days out from each deadline

- Alert the founder as deadlines approach so decisions can be made on time



WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR



Experience:

- Accounting degree or equivalent background in accounting/bookkeeping

- 3+ years of hands-on accounting or bookkeeping experience

- Comfortable owning reconciliation and month-end close

- Experience with QuickBooks Online or similar accounting software



Core Skills:

- Exceptional written English (client-facing invoices and correspondence)

- Proficiency in Google Sheets, Notion, Slack, and Gmail

- Ability to organize and track dozens of small transactions and vendor relationships

- Strong attention to detail and accuracy with numbers



Mindset:

- Self-directed: you manage your own calendar, priorities, and handoff

- Proactive problem-finder: you flag issues before they become problems

- High integrity: you handle financial data and payments with absolute confidentiality and precision

- Collaborative: you're comfortable working with the founder and occasional freelancers



Nice-to-haves:

- Familiarity with contract-to-cash workflows

- Vendor rate negotiation experience



WHAT YOU WILL GAIN

- Clear ownership: You own financial operations end-to-end, not just data entry

- Strategic visibility: Weekly one-on-ones with the founder mean you see the bigger picture

- Fast learning curve: You'll touch invoicing, AR, AP, reconciliation, cash flow, and vendor management—not a siloed task

- Flexible schedule: Choose your preferred daytime PHT window; asynchronous by default

- Professional growth: You'll learn how a real business manages cash and vendor relationships

- Stability: Full-time role with consistent founder check-ins and clear priorities

- Remote-friendly: Structured touchpoints only, no meeting hell

- Impact: Your work directly affects cash flow and keeps operations running



HOW TO APPLY



1. Fill out the intake form at: 

2. Reply with:

   - Your resume (or work history summary)

   - A note about why you're interested in this role

   - Your preferred schedule (which PHT window works best?)



We review applications as they come in and move quickly for strong fits.



TAGS / KEYWORDS



Bookkeeping, Finance Operations, Accounting, QuickBooks Online, Invoicing, Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Reconciliation, Cash Flow Analysis, Vendor Management, Month-End Close, Contract Management, Financial Reporting, Remote Philippines, Day Shift, Full-Time, Operations Coordinator, Notion, Google Sheets, Freelancer Management, Small Business Finance

title: Instagram DM Outreach Specialist — UK Fitness Niche (Part-Time, Long-Term)
description:
Hi! I run a video editing agency for UK fitness coaches and I'm hiring a reliable Virtual Assistant to handle cold DM outreach on Instagram across two of my brand accounts.

English requirement (read first):

You MUST be able to write fluent, natural-sounding English. This role involves writing a personalized opening line for each prospect, and the message has to read like a real native English speaker wrote it. Generic copy-paste DMs will not work. If your written English is not excellent, please do not apply.

What you'll do:

Each morning I'll send you 1–3 source Instagram accounts (other UK fitness coaches with big followings). Your job is to:



Open those accounts and scroll through their followers (and/or who they follow)

Find UK-based fitness coaches who match the criteria below

DM each prospect using my template, with a personalized opening line referencing their content



How to pick good prospects from the source accounts:



UK-based (check bio/location/content references)

1,000–50,000 followers

Posts regularly (active in the last 2 weeks)

Personal brand/coach (not a gym, brand, or company page)

Fitness/coaching niche (not nutritionist, physio, yoga unless they coach)



Daily flow:



3 sessions per day, ~45 mins each, working UK time, Monday–Friday only

Sessions: 8am UK / 1pm UK / 8pm UK (= 3pm / 8pm / 3am Manila)

Volume: starts at ~15 DMs/day in week 1, ramps to 100–120 DMs/day across both accounts by week 4

Log every DM in a Google Sheet (provided) so we don't double-message anyone

WhatsApp summary at end of each day (numbers sent, any issues)

Pause and notify me immediately if any IG warning or restriction appears



Important — what you will NOT do:



You will NOT open or read any incoming DMs/replies. I handle ALL replies myself.

If you a
 open a reply, mark it as unread immediately.

You will not book sales calls or message anyone outside the daily brief.



Personalization example:

Look at the prospect's last 2–3 posts and reference one specifically.

GOOD:



"Hey [name], loved your recent reel on macro tracking — solid breakdown. Quick question — are you editing your videos yourself?"



BAD:



"Hey, love your content!"



If you can't write the GOOD example in fluent English, this role isn't for you.

What I'm looking for:



Excellent written English (essential)

Stable internet

Phone or laptop (phone preferred — safer for IG accounts)

Reliable schedule — Mon–Fri, UK hours including the late evening session

Previous IG outreach or social media VA experience preferred

Follows a written brief without going off-script



Pay:

$320/month flat, paid weekly via Wise every Friday ($80/week)

Hours:

~12 hours per week (3 sessions/day × ~45 mins × 5 days)

Trial:

2-week paid trial. If it's a good fit, ongoing long-term role.

To apply, send a 2-minute Loom video (
 — free) answering:



Have you done Instagram outreach for a client before? Tell me about it.

Imagine you're DMing a UK fitness coach with 5k followers whose last reel was about post-workout nutrition. Write me an actual personalized opening line you'd send them.

Confirm you can work UK hours (8am / 1pm / 8pm UK), Mon–Fri.



Applications without a Loom will not be considered.

Looking to hire this week.
